Summary:
Quick discovery focused on where Evercrest can host inference for customer-facing fraud detection and document ingestion workflows. Main concerns: data residency for EU/US customers, log retention and PII redaction, key management (KMS/HSM) and contractual requirements around subprocessors and auditability. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs; wants an ops playbook and a short benchmark for latency and throughput.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and what triggers sensitive data flows
- High-level choices: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment modes
- Crypto keys, KMS, and egress controls
- Audit logs, SIEM integration, and retention windows
- Compliance needs: GDPR DSARs, HIPAA overlap for certain products, financial regs and internal audit evidence
- Next steps and benchmark plan

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect, occasional misnames) ---
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey all thanks for joining, appreciate the time. I think Jonah and I are on from Redwood, who do we have from Evercrest?
[00:06] Lydia Park: Hi I'm Lydia, head of platform, Carlos is our CISO, Hannah is our cloud arch and Samir is compliance, thanks for doing this.
[00:12] Maya Patel: Great, quick agenda — understand your constraints, data residency and compliance, and talk through hosting options and next steps. Jonah's going to cover performance/ops considerations.
[00:20] Jonah Kim: Yeah hi everyone, quick note — i'll try to call out when something is a runtime detail vs policy.
[00:26] Carlos Montenegro: Our main ask today is to know what we can do without moving to full on-prem. We have EU customers and US ones, and legal is picky about logs leaving EU.
[00:34] Samir Rao: Also interested in PII redaction in logs, audit evidence, and how Redwood supports e-discovery and DSARs.
[00:40] Maya Patel: Totally. Very common. Just to ground this — can you sketch current traffic patterns and where sensitive data enters the flow?
[00:48] Hannah Lee: Sure — 80% of calls are short lookups for fraud signals, low token counts, but we also have a batch document ingestion job that sends longer sequences occasionally — OCR'd statements, KYC docs. Some of those contain SSNs and other PII. We currently route EU user data to eu-1 region, US to us-east.
[01:05] Jonah Kim: Good, makes sense. For the Hosted offering we have region-locking so you can keep inference and logs in eu-1 or us-east, but there are nuances around control plane metadata.
[01:17] Lydia Park: By control plane you mean the management layer? Is any customer data in the control plane?
[01:21] Maya Patel: Short answer — minimal. We keep routing metadata, model version pointers, metrics, and anonymized telemetry. We can provide a control plane isolation option for Private deployments so that even that metadata is in your VPC.
[01:35] Carlos Montenegro: What about logs — request/response logs? We can't send raw request text containing PII to third-party processors.
[01:41] Jonah Kim: Right — out of the box Hosted stores request logs for debugging and for quality monitoring, retention default is 30 days. But we have redaction features and the ability to disable storing responses entirely. With Dedicated you get customer-isolated logging and retention policies, and with Private deployment the logs never leave your network unless you configure forwarding.
[01:58] Samir Rao: For audit we need append-only audit trails for admin actions and model rollouts, and we need the ability to hand over evidence in a war room scenario.
[02:05] Maya Patel: We expose audit logs via SIEM connectors (syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) and can provide signed export bundles for audits. For higher-assurance we offer HSM-backed key material and support for customer-managed keys via KMS integration.
[02:20] Hannah Lee: Can you clarify the KMS flow — do you manage the keys or can we bring our own? We have a couple of HSM-backed keys in Azure Key Vault currently.
[02:26] Jonah Kim: You can bring your own keys (BYOK) for encryption at rest and for certain signing operations. For Dedicated we support customer KMS integration, and for Private we can plug directly into your HSM if network policy allows. One caveat: some ephemeral runtime caches (KV cache) are encrypted but keys may be ephemeral — we document where keys are persistent vs ephemeral.
[02:46] Lydia Park: How do you handle data residency for backups and logs — there's a legal requirement here that backups containing EU data stay in EU.
[02:52] Maya Patel: Backups and snapshots can be region-locked for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be configured for region residency but our standard multi-region backups are off by default for regulated customers — we work through contractual terms.
[03:05] Carlos Montenegro: Can you give us examples of customers who stayed Hosted vs moved to Dedicated for compliance reasons?
[03:10] Maya Patel: Sure — a few fintechs initially used Hosted with region locking and strict retention, and later moved to Dedicated when they wanted total isolation for logs and dedicated GPU pools. We can share redacted reference examples.
[03:22] Samir Rao: We're particularly worried about DSARs — if a EU user requests all personal data, does Redwood help produce the data?
[03:28] Jonah Kim: We can help with exports: request/response logs, audit trails, and metadata. For Hosted that's a support-assisted flow and we can provide exports within SLA per contract. For Dedicated/Private you can self-serve exports. Note: if responses are not stored (you disable), that affects what can be pulled later.
[03:44] Hannah Lee: Follow-up on that — we want to avoid storing raw responses with customer PII in logs. What are options?
[03:50] Maya Patel: Options: 1) disable response logging, 2) enable automatic PII redaction for known patterns (SSNs, dob, etc), 3) tokenization or field-level masking in your application before sending. We recommend a combination.
[04:05] Lydia Park: Are the redaction rules customizable? For finance we have proprietary field types.
[04:09] Jonah Kim: Yes, you can supply custom regexes/field lists for our redaction pipeline for Dedicated and Private. Hosted allows custom rules via a managed config but that requires a security review.
[04:21] Maya Patel: Also worth calling out — our Optimize tooling flags quality regression from prompt changes, so we keep evals and prompts separate from logs for privacy-preserving monitoring.
[04:30] Carlos Montenegro: On legal side there's interest in subprocessors. Do you publish a subprocessor list and notify for changes?
[04:36] Maya Patel: Yes we publish the subprocessor list and we can provide change notification in contract for enterprise customers. We'll also provide DPA language for EU customers.
[04:44] Samir Rao: HIPAA — a couple of our partners have PHI in attachments, this is edge but may be in scope. Is Redwood able to support HIPAA BAA?
[04:52] Jonah Kim: We do support BAAs for specific deployments — typically Private or Dedicated with stricter isolation and contractual controls. Hosted can be covered in some cases but you'd want to validate the data flows first.
[05:06] Lydia Park: Latency — we need sub-150ms p99 for the fraud lookup path. Is that realistic on Hosted?
[05:12] Jonah Kim: For short lookups, yes in many regions Hosted can meet sub-150ms p99 with right model choice and transient batching disabled. But real numbers depend on model size, tokenization, and your network hop. For guaranteed p99 you'd probably go Dedicated colocated near your services, or Private in your VPC.
[05:28] Hannah Lee: If we choose Dedicated, how are upgrades/rollouts handled? We need canary and rollback.
[05:33] Maya Patel: Dedicated supports canary rollouts and A/B routing. We maintain model versioning and you can pin routes to versions; rollbacks are automatic on error thresholds. Those audit trails are included.
[05:45] Carlos Montenegro: What about encryption in transit and at rest? Any customer-managed options?
[05:49] Jonah Kim: TLS 1.2+ in transit, and at rest via provider-managed disks. For customer-managed encryption keys we integrate with major KMSs for Dedicated and Private.
[06:00] Lydia Park: One more: egress. Our compliance folks want to control any data leaving EU. If Redwood calls out to a third-party tokenizer or external subservice, how is that surfaced?
[06:09] Maya Patel: We list all subprocessors and external services in the security pack. Tokenization is done in-process in the runtime, we don't send raw text to separate tokenizer services. But any optional integrations (e.g., third-party eval/ops tools) are documented and can be disabled.
[06:26] Samir Rao: What's the retention model for ephemeral caches like KV cache? Do you persist that to disk?
[06:31] Jonah Kim: KV cache is in-memory for inference, but for longer sessions we may persist encrypted snapshots for warm start. Those snapshots can be region-locked or disabled. For Dedicated/Private snapshots remain under your control.
[06:45] Hannah Lee: For the benchmarking — we want to run our dataset for throughput and p99. How much do we need to mirror?
[06:50] Jonah Kim: For meaningful p99 numbers, mirror representative traffic for at least several hours, focusing on peak windows. We'll provide a runbook. We can do a dry run on Redwood test cluster first to tune batch settings, then do a Dedicated benchmark with your infra.
[07:06] Lydia Park: Cost question — what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated for consistent qps?
[07:11] Maya Patel: It depends on GPU types and utilization. Hosted is usage-based (per-token + per-embedding units). Dedicated has a reserved capacity model with monthly commit but you get lower unit costs at scale and more predictable p99. We'll send a sample TCO sheet.
[07:25] Carlos Montenegro: Anything specific to EU data residency that you recommend contractually?
[07:29] Maya Patel: Region locking for storage, contractual DPA with EU SCCs or equivalent, and explicit clauses for subprocessor notifications and audit rights. For the highest assurance, Dedicated or Private with customer-managed keys and SIEM integration.
[07:44] Samir Rao: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates we can review?
[07:48] Maya Patel: Yes we'll send the pack.
[07:51] Hannah Lee: Operational question — on log forwarding, do you support structured logs with redaction and JSON schema so our SIEM can ingest fields reliably?
[07:58] Jonah Kim: Yes we emit structured JSON logs and support field-level redaction and custom schema mapping.
[08:04] Lydia Park: Great. One last thing — if we do Private, what's the maintenance overhead? Patches, kernel updates, model onboarding, etc.
[08:11] Maya Patel: Private can be offered as either self-managed or Redwood-managed. If self-managed you handle infra patches and we provide release notes + tools. If Redwood-managed, we handle orchestration and updates under a managed service agreement with maintenance windows and change control.
[08:28] Carlos Montenegro: Ok, actionable next steps?
[08:31] Maya Patel: We'll send security pack, subprocessor list, and a benchmark runbook. Jonah will draft the benchmark plan and we'll stand up a Dedicated trial if you want.
[08:39] Jonah Kim: I'll follow up with required infra spec and a template for anonymized traffic. We'll also propose a 2-hour benchmark window.
[08:45] Lydia Park: We'll aim to get the sample traffic to you by Friday. If this goes well legal will want contract language around region locking and data processing.
[08:55] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone — i'll email the materials and set up the benchmark planning call.

--- End of transcript ---
